run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:04:52Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alerting signal is real but low-grade: in 2026-11-17T23:14:44Z–2026-11-18T00:14:44Z traces_span_metrics_calls_total reports 20.29 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for service_name="frontend-proxy" on span_name="ingress" (vs 24771 UNSET) and 0 errors on "router frontend egress". The frontend-proxy log shows those errors are the proxy's own `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` responses for requests routed to the frontend: 11 occurrences 23:40:45–23:54:41 and 9 more 23:56:44–00:08:31 (pod-local log timestamps). The frontend itself records zero error spans and normal homepage latency (725.5 GET / spans, 671.7 of them ≤100 ms), all otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and the proxy ingress span rate stays flat at ~7–8.9 spans/s, so no load surge or frontend crash is observable. The only object change in the window is a load-generator Deployment rollout at 23:55:42Z (new ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd, old 57ffcd644 scaled 1→0), and ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds the fault-injection flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage switched on (defaultVariant "on", variants off:0/on:100, "Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests") while all other flags are off; that ConfigMap is the leading candidate object. Two things keep the conclusion partial: the declared homepage flood is not visible (only ~319 of 9904 proxy lines in 23:54:53–00:09:38 are `GET /`, about 3 % of traffic, and 503s already start at 23:40:45, before the 23:55:42 rollout), and neither the moment the flag changed nor the frontend's own side of the resets is observable in this Run.

claims.text: For the hour 2026-11-17T23:14:44Z–2026-11-18T00:14:44Z, traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name="frontend-proxy" reports span_name="ingress" status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 20.294 and STATUS_CODE_UNSET increase 24771, while span_name="router frontend egress" reports STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0 and STATUS_CODE_UNSET increase 24794.3 — the proxy's error spans occur only on its server-side ingress spans.

Both frontend-proxy error series exist as separate series with span_kind SPAN_KIND_SERVER (span_name "ingress") and SPAN_KIND_CLIENT (span_name "router frontend egress"), status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR, exported via the spanmetricsconnector from job otel-collector.

frontend-proxy error spans are non-zero in every 5-minute window sampled from 23:41:44Z through 00:11:44Z (values between 1.10 and 7.78 errors per 5m) and are 0 in the final sampled window ending 00:13:44Z; the same query shows frontend, accounting and payment error increases of 0 for the hour.

The frontend-proxy pod's access log shows 11 responses of the exact form `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` for GET paths routed to the `frontend` cluster between 23:40:45.642Z and 23:54:41.653Z (e.g. /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, /), i.e. the proxy returned 503 because the upstream frontend terminated the connection before response start.

Nine more identical `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` responses appear in the same pod's log between 23:56:44.307Z and 00:08:31.650Z, and among 9904 log lines read for 23:54:53Z–00:09:38Z these nine were the only 5xx responses matched by the pattern `HTTP/1.1. 5xx`.

The frontend service records STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0 for all of its operations in the hour (GET, GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route …, grpc.oteldemo.* calls, tcp.connect), while those operations ran between 725 and 21371 times each — no frontend-side span was marked failed.

frontend span_name="GET /" duration histogram for the hour contains 725.5 spans with 452.6 at ≤10 ms, 513.4 at ≤50 ms, 671.7 at ≤100 ms, 711.3 at ≤200 ms and 719.4 at ≤400 ms, so homepage requests were answered quickly with only a handful slower than 400 ms.

The frontend-proxy ingress span rate is flat across the window: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress"}[2m])) evaluates between 6.96 and 8.93 spans/s at every 2-minute point from 23:36:44Z to 00:10:44Z, with no step change.

All 21 otel-demo pods (including frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 started 23:23:54Z and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth started 23:23:53Z) are phase Running with Ready/ContainersReady True, restartCount 0 and empty lastState for every container.

The only otel-demo events inside the authorized window are the load-generator Deployment rollout at 23:55:42–23:55:43Z: ScalingReplicaSet load-generator up 84895ffcd 0→1 and down 57ffcd644 1→0, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/load-generator-84895ffcd and SuccessfulDelete/load-generator-57ffcd644, Pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started and Pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 Killing.

Two load-generator ReplicaSets exist, load-generator-57ffcd644 created 23:23:52Z and load-generator-84895ffcd created 23:55:42Z, both owned by Deployment load-generator — the 23:55:42 rollout replaced the pod template rather than restarting in place.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds key demo.flagd.json with fault-injection flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage: state ENABLED, defaultVariant "on", description "Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests.", variants {"off":0,"on":100}; every other listed flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

Deployment load-generator (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2) runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator with LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080, LOCUST_USERS=50, LOCUST_SPAWN_RATE=5, LOCUST_AUTOSTART=true and FLAGD_HOST=flagd, so its traffic is generated against frontend-proxy and it reads flags from flagd.

In 9904 frontend-proxy log lines read for 23:54:53Z–00:09:38Z only 319 are `GET / HTTP` requests (≈21.6/min, about 3 % of logged requests), and the load-generator pod's log over 23:55:45Z–00:09:37Z contains 287 lines matching "flood|index page|homepage" out of 7131 lines — homepage requests were a small minority, not a flood.
Deployment frontend defines limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi and requests cpu 50m / memory 100Mi for its single container, and that container has no readinessProbe or livenessProbe.

Leading candidate: the fault-injection setting loadGeneratorFloodHomepage = "on" (value 100) held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config put extra homepage load on the frontend, whose server then terminated in-flight connections, producing the proxy's 503 UC responses and hence the frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and the RequestErrorRate alert; the load-generator rollout at 23:55:42Z is the only object change seen in the window and no other object applies a fault to frontend or frontend-proxy.

Alternative: the 503 UC errors are a chronic connection-reuse race between the proxy's upstream connection pool and the frontend HTTP server — the 503s arrive in pairs on the same seconds (23:43:27 twice, 23:45:21 twice, 23:48:56/57, 23:57:27 twice), which is what several requests multiplexed on one closing upstream connection produce; the alert then fires because its condition is error rate above 0, not because of a new fault.

Alternative: the frontend container's very low cpu limit (100m) could throttle or stall its server enough to drop connections; this is unverified because no CPU/throttling metric is present in the available Prometheus series, and the observed homepage latency does not show sustained slowness.

Against a load-driven cause: the frontend-proxy ingress span rate is flat at ~7–8.9 spans/s for the whole sampled period, and the declared homepage flood is not visible — only ~3 % of logged requests are `GET /` and homepage requests are answered in ≤100 ms in most cases.

Against the rollout as trigger: 503 UC errors are already logged at 23:40:45Z, 23:43:27Z, 23:44:53Z and 23:45:21Z, i.e. about 15 minutes before the load-generator ReplicaSet was replaced at 23:55:42Z.

Rejected: the frontend-proxy errors were caused by failed downstream calls inside the frontend (ad, cart, checkout, product-catalog, recommendation, currency, payment). The proxy's client span "router frontend egress" shows zero error increase, the frontend's own spans record zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and the failures are 503 UC responses in which the connection was terminated before any response started.

Rejected: the frontend-proxy pod was itself broken (crash, eviction, OOM, failed rollout). The pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState, no previous container instance, and no Pod-level Warning events or Pod replacement events exist for it in the window.

Compare the frontend-proxy upstream idle/keep-alive settings with the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive timeout, since the 503 UC response flag and the paired failures point at requests being sent on a connection the upstream closed; if confirmed, this is a configuration-level noise source rather than an application fault.

Verify with the owners whether flagd flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is intended to be "on" in this environment, and if not, switch it to "off" and observe whether the frontend-proxy 503 UC entries and the error-span rate disappear.

Align the RequestErrorRate alert with the observed noise floor (for example a non-zero threshold or a longer evaluation window) because the observed condition is ~20 error spans per hour out of ~24791 ingress spans, i.e. a single transient 503 is enough to satisfy an error-rate-above-0 rule.

gaps: The alert's own expression and window are unknown: a list_prometheus_rules query with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data with no rules, so the reported current value 0.01111111111111111 cannot be reproduced from any metric series accessible here (only traces_span_metrics_calls_total, traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket and kube-state metrics).

The declared flood itself was not observed: request rate and homepage share show no flood, and no log line states that a flood ran. The gap is whether flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage="on" is actually acted on by the running load-generator.

The moment the loadGeneratorFloodHomepage flag changed is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run and ConfigMap flagd-config exposes only creationTimestamp 2026-11-17T23:23:52Z and resourceVersion 1600457, neither of which dates the flag edit.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 returned status read with bytes_read 0 and no content (queries listed as no_data in this Run), so the frontend's side of the upstream_reset_before_response_started events is unknown.

A fetch_pod_logs query for the flagd pod flagd-869c45cb9d-s58zn (containers init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) returned no lines (status no_data), so flag-file reload events and flag evaluation errors could not be checked.

Trace data is incomplete after ~23:38Z: traces_search for frontend-proxy and for frontend in later windows returned no traces (status no_data), and tag-filtered searches for this incident (http.status_code=500, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR, error=true) returned no traces, so the error spans themselves could not be retrieved by trace_id.

What changed in the load-generator pod template at the 23:55:42Z rollout is unknown: only Deployment revision 2 and the new pod-template-hash 84895ffcd are visible, and the replaced pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 has been deleted so its logs and spec could not be read.

No CPU or throttling metric exists among the queryable series (a get_metric_names query for http_* and for traces_*/rpc_*/app_* returned only the two traces_span_metrics series), so the low frontend cpu limit (100m) cannot be confirmed or ruled out as a contributor to the connection terminations.

The data-recorders namespace appears only in events (Deployment/StatefulSet/Job/PVC activity including Pod FailedScheduling and PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete); a kubernetes_jq_query for Deployments in data-recorders returned no data, so that namespace's workloads were not examined and are unrelated to this finding on present evidence.

Sporadic error spans also appear on ad (3.05/h), fraud-detection (3.05/h) and recommendation (4.06/h) in the same hour; their own logs and causes were not investigated, so whether they share a cause with the frontend-proxy 503s remains unknown.
next_steps: Retrieve the frontend-proxy upstream connection-pool configuration (idle timeout, max requests per connection, HTTP protocol version) and compare it with the frontend server's keep-alive timeout.

Check the frontend container's CPU throttling and memory history over 2026-11-17T23:35Z–2026-11-18T00:15Z from a source that exposes container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total or working-set metrics, which this Run's metric set does not.

Read the frontend process logs from a source that retains them (the pod currently emits nothing on stdout) for the exact times 23:40:45Z, 23:43:27Z, 23:45:21Z, 23:48:56Z, 23:57:27Z, 00:02:56Z, 00:04:26Z and 00:08:31Z.

Confirm with the environment owners whether flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is meant to be "on"; if it is, capture a baseline of frontend-proxy 503 UC counts with it off to decide whether the alert reflects the injection or background connection-reuse noise.
Ask the platform team for the alerting rule behind RequestErrorRate so the reported 0.0111 value can be reproduced against traces_span_metrics_calls_total.
Consider raising the alert threshold above the observed ~20 errors/hour noise floor or extending its window, so single transient 503s do not page.
